signature.name: Cadbury World
signature.detail: A chocolate-themed museum that is Birmingham's most distinctive visitor attraction, tracing the story of Cadbury and offering plenty of tasting along the way. Book tickets online in advance, as timed slots sell out in school holidays, and allow a half day; it sits in Bournville, reachable by train from the city centre.

signature.name: Birmingham Museum and Art Gallery
signature.detail: The city's flagship museum, home to a celebrated Pre-Raphaelite art collection and wide-ranging displays on Birmingham's history. Entry is free, so it is an easy must-see; check opening days before you go as galleries sometimes close for rotation.

signature.name: St Philip's Cathedral
signature.detail: A compact but striking cathedral in the heart of the city, known for its Burne-Jones stained-glass windows. It is free to enter and makes a peaceful pause between the shops; visit on a weekday morning for the quietest experience.

signature.name: Birmingham Canal Navigations
signature.detail: Birmingham has more miles of canal than Venice, and the city-centre stretches around Brindleyplace are the easiest to explore on foot. Walk the towpaths in the late afternoon or stop at a waterside cafe; the routes are flat and free.

signature.name: Bullring
signature.detail: The city's landmark shopping hub, crowned by the futuristic Selfridges building, and a good orientation point for central Birmingham. It is free to wander and busiest at weekends, so come on a weekday for a calmer browse.

signature.name: University of Birmingham
signature.detail: A grand red-brick campus with a distinctive clock tower, worth a stroll if you enjoy architecture and green space. It is a short train ride from the centre at University station; the grounds are open and free to walk.

transport: Bus or tram around $3 a ride; day tickets around $8
